Resolves #21646

🌿 On a machine with eighteen cores, `build-all` can no longer keep four builds that share nothing waiting in line.

`npm run build-all` runs dev threads, prod threads, `dist/esm` and the docs JSON together, through a pool that runs a quarter of the cores at once. That is four on the M5 Max and one on a 4-core CI runner, where the sequence stays. `check-dist-paths`, the docs copies and the build-id stamps read the pool's output and run after it. That includes `dist/esm`'s copy of `docs/output`, which `esmodules.mjs` now leaves to `build-all` (`--no-docs-output`). `all.mjs` gains the pool (`runSteps`, `startStep`) and drops its three sequential blocks. #21642, the operator's 30 s outcome, stays open: this is its first lever.

Evidence: L3 (real `npm run build-all` runs on the M5 Max, A/B against `dev`'s sequential `all.mjs` from a fresh-checkout `docs/output`, every output file hashed) → L3 required (AC-1 and AC-2 are observable only on a real build). Residual: none for #21646.

## AC Evidence

| AC | Evidence |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | outside-CI: both builds start from removed dist trees and a fresh-checkout `docs/output` (only the tracked `class-hierarchy.json`), with one build id. The 15,370 files outside `dist/esm/docs/output` hash identically. `dist/esm/docs/output` holds the run's 842 docs JSON files, byte-identical to `docs/output`; `dev` copies 1 there (see Deltas) |
| AC-2 | outside-CI: alternating runs on the M5 Max. Sequential 57.9, 70.2 and 97.4 s (median 70.2); parallel 36.3, 53.4 and 40.1 s (median 40.1). The 1-minute load ran from 12.9 to 22.3. The first A/B, before RA-1, had medians of 62.3 and 39.5 s |
| AC-3 | CI-covered: `buildId.spec.mjs`. A failed `esmodules.mjs` or `seo/copy.mjs` step exits 7 and publishes no id. The threads invocations are pinned as `-e dev` and `-e prod`, and `esmodules.mjs` runs with `--no-docs-output` while `dist/esm` receives `docs/output` after the steps |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: the `build-all` job |

## Deltas from ticket

`dist/esm/docs/output` now holds the docs JSON of the same run. On `dev`, `esmodules.mjs` copied `docs/output` before `generate-docs-json` ran, so `dist/esm`'s docs app read the previous build's JSON, or in a fresh checkout neither the `all.json` nor the `structure.json` it requests. Moving that copy after the pool closes RA-1's race and this staleness together. #21646's AC-1 is amended to match.

## Test Evidence

- The A/B harness and both manifests stay on the shared machine. The first A/B removed `docs/output` before each arm, so `esmodules.mjs`'s copy never fired and RA-1's race stayed out of its hashes. The second starts from the checkout's `docs/output`.

## Post-Merge Validation

- [ ] `publish.mjs prepare --rehearse` on `dev` reports every gate ✅. It refuses a branch, so #21033's step 4 runs it on cut day.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: **Concurrent `fs.copySync` vs `fs.writeFile` (`O_TRUNC`) race on `docs/output/` (`buildScripts/build/esmodules.mjs:124-127` vs `buildScripts/docs/generateDocsJson.mjs:363-468`).**
  - `all.mjs:217-218` assumes every pooled step *"writes its own tree (`dist/esm`, `docs/output`) and reads only the sources."* While `esmBuildGraph.mjs:62` excludes `/docs/output/` from `emitFiles()`, `esmodules.mjs:124-127` then runs:
    ```js
    const docsOutputPath = path.resolve(root, 'docs/output');
    if (fs.existsSync(docsOutputPath)) {
        fs.copySync(docsOutputPath, path.resolve(root, outputBasePath, 'docs/output'))
    }
    ```
  - Because `docs/output/class-hierarchy.json` is tracked in git (`git ls-files docs/output` = `1`), `fs.existsSync(docsOutputPath)` is `true` on every real checkout (and on any second build ~1,000 `docs/output/**/*.json` files already sit on disk). On 16+ core hosts (`limit = 4`, or 8+ core hosts under `-e esm` where `steps` has 2 items), `esmodules.mjs` finishes `emitFiles()` at ~5–6 s — right as `generateDocsJson.mjs` finishes `parse(options)` and fires `writeJSON('./docs/output/all.json')` + `Promise.all(writePromises)` using non-atomic `fs.writeFile` (`O_TRUNC`, `docletPipeline/index.mjs:55`).
  - Depending on sub-second scheduling: (1) if `esmodules.mjs` copies before `writeJSON` starts, `dist/esm/docs/output` gets stale pre-build JSON (or only `class-hierarchy.json` on a fresh clone, never `all.json` / `structure.json`); (2) if `esmodules.mjs` copies during `Promise.all(writePromises)`, `fs.copySync` reads 0-byte truncated or half-written JSON files mid-write (or hits `ENOENT`/partial state); (3) in the AC-1 A/B benchmark where `docs/output` was removed beforehand, `esmodules.mjs` (~5.2 s) beat `generateDocsJson`'s first `writeJSON` (~6 s) in both sequential and parallel runs, leaving `dist/esm/docs/output` absent from both manifests and hiding the race.
